title: Machine learning in cardiovascular magnetic resonance: basic concepts and applications.
task: Overview of AI across acquisition, reconstruction, segmentation, diagnosis, prognosis
outcomes_summary: Early field review highlighting strongest near-term gains in automated segmentation/quantification and calling for multicenter trials and open methods.
validation_or_trial_status: Review; emphasizes need for controlled multicenter evaluation

title: Quantitative cardiac MRI.
task: Quantitative CMR and ML-ready biomarkers
outcomes_summary: Frames quantitative CMR as the substrate for workflow efficiency, earlier detection, monitoring, and risk stratification using ML.

title: Deep Learning for Quantitative Cardiac MRI.
task: Deep learning methods for quantitative CMR
outcomes_summary: Summarizes state-of-the-art deep learning for quantitative CMR analysis and key translational limitations.

title: The Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance-A Comprehensive Review.
task: AI across the CMR pipeline
outcomes_summary: Reviews AI applications from image acquisition through prognostication, useful for broad background framing.

title: Present and Future Innovations in AI and Cardiac MRI.
task: Workflow innovation and future AI-enabled CMR practice
outcomes_summary: Highlights self-driving scanners, inline analysis, and integration with multimodal data as the next phase of CMR AI.

title: The role of artificial intelligence in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.
task: Clinical applications of AI in CMR
outcomes_summary: Synthesizes acquisition, prescription, segmentation, scar detection, outcome prediction, and adoption barriers.

title: Artificial intelligence in cardiac radiology.
task: Cardiac CT/MR automation and reporting support
outcomes_summary: Useful contextual review of automation, reporting, reconstruction, and radiologist-facing AI across CT and MRI.

title: Artificial intelligence in cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging.
task: Current state of AI-enabled CMR
outcomes_summary: Concise recent review spanning segmentation, tissue characterization, non-contrast fibrosis assessment, diagnosis, and prognosis.

title: Radiomics applications in cardiac imaging: a comprehensive review.
task: Radiomics for diagnosis, risk stratification, and follow-up
outcomes_summary: Summarizes radiomics opportunities and recurring limitations, especially lack of standardization and external validation.

title: Challenges in clinical translation of cardiac magnetic resonance imaging radiomics in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy: a narrative review.
task: Radiomics translation in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy
outcomes_summary: Details practical workflow and translational bottlenecks for MRI radiomics in HCM, DCM, and myocarditis.

title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac Amyloidosis: A Focus on Diagnosis and Clinical Application.
task: AI-enabled diagnosis and management of cardiac amyloidosis
outcomes_summary: Useful disease-focused synthesis across ECG, echo, scintigraphy, and CMR, while noting need for prospective trials.

title: Imaging for the diagnosis of acute myocarditis: can artificial intelligence improve diagnostic performance?
task: AI for myocarditis diagnosis on CMR
outcomes_summary: Concludes the evidence base is still small, poorly characterized, and missing robust disease-control cohorts despite promise.

title: From Compressed-Sensing to Artificial Intelligence-Based Cardiac MRI Reconstruction.
task: AI-based CMR reconstruction
outcomes_summary: Key review on accelerated acquisition/reconstruction, highlighting technical hurdles before routine deployment.

title: Synergistic multi-contrast cardiac magnetic resonance image reconstruction.
task: Multi-contrast reconstruction for parametric mapping
outcomes_summary: Explains how low-rank, model-based, and emerging DL approaches can shorten multi-contrast mapping acquisitions.

title: Precision measurement of cardiac structure and function in cardiovascular magnetic resonance using machine learning.
study_type: Multicenter retrospective development and validation study
task: Automated volumetric segmentation and functional quantification
outcomes_summary: Trained on 1,923 scans and validated with 109 scan-rescan patients plus 1,277 routine scans; machine analysis was 20 s per patient, more precise than clinicians, and could reduce trial sample sizes by 46% for LVEF endpoints.
validation_or_trial_status: Independent multisite validation with scanner/vendor/pathology diversity

title: Semi-supervised segmentation of cardiac chambers from LGE-CMR using feature consistency awareness.
task: LGE chamber segmentation with limited labels
outcomes_summary: Semi-supervised segmentation achieved Dice around 88-91% on atrial and 87-89% on ventricular tasks using only 10-20% labeled data.
validation_or_trial_status: Technical validation; dataset-level rather than prospective clinical validation

title: Automated segmentation of long and short axis DENSE cardiovascular magnetic resonance for myocardial strain analysis using spatio-temporal convolutional neural networks.
task: Automated segmentation for DENSE strain analysis
outcomes_summary: Used 360 short-axis and 124 long-axis slices; automated strain showed good to excellent agreement with manual pipelines and external reproducibility testing.

title: Deep learning based automated left ventricle segmentation and flow quantification in 4D flow cardiac MRI.
task: 4D flow LV segmentation and hemodynamic quantification
outcomes_summary: Best model achieved Dice 84.5% and enabled LV volume, EF, kinetic energy, and flow-component quantification without separate cine MRI.
validation_or_trial_status: Single in-house dataset with uncertainty analysis

title: Cardiac function assessment with deep-learning-based automatic segmentation of free-running four-dimensional whole-heart cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
task: Free-running whole-heart 4D segmentation
outcomes_summary: Automatic segmentation within under a minute achieved Dice 0.86-0.94 and excellent LV metric agreement, supporting adoption of free-running imaging workflows.
validation_or_trial_status: Validated across diverse protocols with complementary geometric and clinical metrics

title: Landmark Detection in Cardiac MRI by Using a Convolutional Neural Network.
study_type: Retrospective multicenter development and hold-out test study
task: Automated landmark detection for scan planning and quantification
outcomes_summary: Trained on 2,329 patients and tested on 531; landmark detection success was 96.6-100% across cine, LGE, and T1 mapping, with inference in 0.6 s on GPU.
validation_or_trial_status: Two-hospital study with deployed scanner workflow

title: Automatic uncertainty-based quality controlled T1 mapping and ECV analysis from native and post-contrast cardiac T1 mapping images using Bayesian vision transformer.
task: Quality-controlled T1 mapping and ECV automation
outcomes_summary: QC model reached AUC 0.927 for failed-segmentation detection, and automated native T1/ECV closely matched manual values (Pearson 0.990 and 0.975).
validation_or_trial_status: Internal validation with explicit uncertainty/QC layer

title: Validation of a deep learning-based software for automated analysis of T2 mapping in cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
task: Automated T2 map segmentation and elevated T2 detection
outcomes_summary: Automated T2 values were non-inferior to expert readings, with sensitivity 83.6-92.8% and specificity 82.5-92.0% for elevated T2 detection.
validation_or_trial_status: Multi-institutional validation of commercial DL software

title: Automated assessment of cardiac pathologies on cardiac MRI using T1-mapping and late gadolinium phase sensitive inversion recovery sequences with deep learning.
task: Pathology detection from T1 mapping and PSIR
outcomes_summary: On hold-out testing, PSIR-based DL yielded 88% accuracy and T1-mapping alone yielded 70% accuracy, showing contrast-free potential but modest specificity.

title: Deep-Learning-Based Preprocessing for Quantitative Myocardial Perfusion MRI.
task: Automated perfusion preprocessing and segmentation
outcomes_summary: Automated pipeline produced myocardial blood-flow values close to manual analysis (ICC 0.89, bias 2.6% of mean MBF), lowering a major barrier to quantitative perfusion CMR.

title: Screening and diagnosis of cardiovascular disease using artificial intelligence-enabled cardiac magnetic resonance imaging.
study_type: Large retrospective development and external validation study
task: Automated CMR screening and diagnosis across multiple diseases
outcomes_summary: Two-stage cine plus LGE system achieved AUC 0.988 for screening and 0.991 for diagnosis, with strong internal and external performance and cardiologist-level or better results for some tasks.
validation_or_trial_status: Internal and external validation; proof-of-concept for scalable computerized CMR interpretation

title: Cardiac magnetic resonance radiomics for disease classification.
task: Classification of HCM, DCM, and normal hearts
outcomes_summary: Radiomics model achieved 91.2% accuracy and AUCs of 0.938-0.966 across normal, DCM, and HCM classes.
validation_or_trial_status: Two public datasets with test-set evaluation

title: Machine Learning to Automatically Differentiate Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy, Cardiac Light Chain, and Cardiac Transthyretin Amyloidosis: A Multicenter CMR Study.
task: Differential diagnosis of HCM versus AL/ATTR amyloidosis
outcomes_summary: Across 56 institutions, staged ML achieved AUCs of 1.00, 0.99, and 0.92 for healthy-vs-disease, HCM-vs-amyloid, and AL-vs-ATTR differentiation.

title: Differentiation of light chain cardiac amyloidosis and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy by ensemble machine learning-based radiomic analysis of cardiac magnetic resonance.
study_type: Retrospective development and hold-out test study
task: Radiomics classification of AL amyloidosis versus HCM
outcomes_summary: Ensemble radiomics model using mapping sequences achieved AUC 0.98 on the hold-out test set for three-way classification versus HCM and controls.
validation_or_trial_status: Internal hold-out test; no external cohort reported

title: Deep learning to diagnose cardiac amyloidosis from cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
task: LGE-based diagnosis of cardiac amyloidosis
outcomes_summary: DL model on LGE images achieved AUC 0.982 and 88% accuracy, similar to a feature-rich ML simulation of expert CMR reading.

title: Differentiating between cardiac amyloidosis and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on non-contrast cine-magnetic resonance images using machine learning-based radiomics.
task: Non-contrast differentiation of amyloidosis versus HCM
outcomes_summary: Combined radiomics plus MR metrics improved discrimination over conventional MR metrics alone (AUC 0.89 vs 0.79).

title: Texture analysis of T2-weighted cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging to discriminate between cardiac amyloidosis and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
task: T2-weighted texture analysis for amyloid vs HCM
outcomes_summary: Texture model achieved AUC 0.915 in training and 0.842 in testing, with performance comparable to LGE for differentiating amyloid from HCM.

title: Machine learning of native T1 mapping radiomics for classification of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy phenotypes.
task: Native T1 radiomics for phenotype classification
outcomes_summary: A six-feature radiomics signature outperformed mean native T1 for distinguishing health, LVH, HCM, and cardiac amyloid phenotypes.
validation_or_trial_status: Internal validation with external testing described in abstract

title: Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy automatic diagnosis using a deep learning approach.
task: Automated LVNC diagnosis from trabecular segmentation
outcomes_summary: U-Net segmentation supported VT% computation and LVNC diagnosis with AUC 0.94, sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.80, and 99.5% clinically valid segmentations in expert review.
validation_or_trial_status: 5-fold cross-validation with specialist clinical validity assessment

title: CNN-KCL: Automatic myocarditis diagnosis using convolutional neural network combined with k-means clustering.
task: Automatic myocarditis diagnosis
outcomes_summary: In a small image-heavy dataset, CNN-KCL reported 97.4% accuracy with 10-fold cross-validation, but external validation was absent.

title: Radiomics analysis of short tau inversion recovery images in cardiac magnetic resonance for the prediction of late gadolinium enhancement in patients with acute myocarditis.
task: Predict LGE from STIR images
outcomes_summary: Ensemble ML predicted LGE presence from STIR with AUC 0.79, NPV 0.81, and could support shorter myocarditis protocols.

title: Interpretable machine learning for automated left ventricular scar quantification in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy patients.
task: Automated scar quantification on LGE CMR
outcomes_summary: Across 2,557 images from 307 HCM patients, automated scar quantification correlated strongly with manual labels (r=0.92) with low bias for %LGE mass.

title: Radiomics and deep learning for myocardial scar screening in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
task: Screening for absence of scar on cine imaging before gadolinium
outcomes_summary: Combined DL-radiomics model outperformed either approach alone, with AUC 0.83 internally and 0.74 externally for identifying patients without scar who might avoid contrast.
validation_or_trial_status: Multi-center/vendor development plus external validation cohort

title: Genetics of myocardial interstitial fibrosis in the human heart and association with disease.
task: ML quantification of native myocardial T1 and fibrosis associations
outcomes_summary: ML-based T1 quantification in UK Biobank linked higher T1 to multiple cardiovascular diseases and identified 11 fibrosis-associated loci.
validation_or_trial_status: Large-scale population study; translational biology rather than prospective clinical trial

title: Noninvasive assessment of organ-specific and shared pathways in multi-organ fibrosis using T1 mapping.
task: ML quantification of T1 across organs
outcomes_summary: ML-derived T1 mapping linked fibrosis burden across organs to disease and mortality; ≥3 fibrotic organs carried a 3.31-fold mortality increase.

title: DEep LearnIng-based QuaNtification of epicardial adipose tissue predicts MACE in patients undergoing stress CMR.
task: Automated EAT quantification for risk stratification
outcomes_summary: Automated EAT volume independently predicted MACE and improved Harrell C from 0.76 to 0.85 when added to standard stress-CMR risk features, with confirmation in a validation cohort.

title: Benefits of Machine Learning to Predict Survival Using Stress Perfusion CMR and Basic Clinical Information.
task: Survival prediction from stress perfusion CMR plus clinical data
outcomes_summary: Representative study showing ML can improve survival prediction from stress perfusion CMR and basic clinical variables beyond simpler approaches.
validation_or_trial_status: Prognostic modeling study; inspect full text for exact sample size and external-validation details

title: Machine Learning in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Nonlinear Model From Clinical and CMR Features Predicting Cardiovascular Events.
task: Prediction of composite cardiovascular events
outcomes_summary: Using 14 CMR and 23 clinical features, ML achieved AUC 0.830 internally and 0.812 externally, outperforming HCM Risk-SCD and identifying nonlinear risk thresholds for LGE and strain.
validation_or_trial_status: Internal discovery cohort plus external three-center test cohort

title: Multimodal AI to forecast arrhythmic death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
task: Arrhythmic death risk stratification
outcomes_summary: MAARS integrated EHR, reports, and contrast CMR, achieving AUC 0.89 internally and 0.81 externally, markedly outperforming guideline-based risk models.
validation_or_trial_status: Internal and external cohort validation with fairness analysis

title: A Machine Learning Model Using Cardiac CT and MRI Data Predicts Cardiovascular Events in Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease.
task: MACE prediction using CCTA plus stress CMR
outcomes_summary: ML model combining CT and stress CMR achieved AUC 0.86 and validated externally at AUC 0.84 and 0.92, outperforming traditional scores and single-modality models.

title: Prediction of Cardiovascular Events Using Fully Automated Global Longitudinal and Circumferential Strain in Patients Undergoing Stress CMR.
task: Automated strain for event prediction
outcomes_summary: Fully automated rest GLS and stress GCS were feasible in 96% and independently improved MACE prediction, with net reclassification improvement of 15.6%.
validation_or_trial_status: Single-center cohort with long follow-up; no separate external validation in abstract

title: A novel deep learning system for STEMI prognostic prediction from multi-sequence cardiac magnetic resonance.
task: Post-STEMI 2-year MACE prediction from multisequence CMR
outcomes_summary: DeepSTEMI used 610 registry patients for development and 334 external-validation patients, reaching AUC 0.894 and identifying a 20-fold risk difference between predicted high- and low-risk groups.
validation_or_trial_status: External validation across three independent cardiac centers
